newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIA'S NDOLA SEEKS TO RENEW LIME CONTRACTS.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA'S NDOLA SEEKS TO RENEW LIME CONTRACTS.

text.p: Zambia's Ndola Lime company said on Tuesday it was trying to win back export contracts it lost earlier this year to meet Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines lime requirements during a production shortfall.

A company official told Reuters Ndola Lime would have to renegotiate contracts it abandoned with buyers in Namibia, South Africa, Malawi and Zimbabwe, when output dropped due to heavy fuel oil shortages.

"The suspension has left the export market in limbo because at the time we suspended exports we already had confirmed orders which we did not fulfil. We have to renegotiate (the contracts)," the official said.
Ndola Lime was compelled to breach the contracts after its sister company ZCCM, which uses 85 percent of its lime output, started importing heavy fuel oil from South Africa.
Ndola's production fell when the state-run Indeni oil refinery cut its heavy fuel oil supplies from 120 tonnes to 40 tonnes per day.
The low lime output pushed ZCCM copper production down to 21,380 tonnes in April, against an official estimate of 27,057 tonnes. Copper production in March was 32,051 tonnes.
The fuel shortage forced the closure of ZCCM's Mufulira smelter, its Nchanga open pit and two furnaces at Nkana smelter for the first two weeks of April.
